A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iNews study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotations from 291 participants, regression analyses, a 20-participant qualitative study, a modality pilot, and zero-shot and few-shot model evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports annotation-quality outcomes and comparisons of its participants' calibration ratings with ANET norms.

M1.justification: The persona-prompting procedure, few-shot construction, and regression specifications are retained. The Plutchik-to-Ekman attribution correction leaves the emotion options in Figure 8 unchanged. The added manual and quality-control details document the existing study rather than establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds the original US ANET normative ratings as comparison data for calibration evaluation (Table 1). V1 already used the same three sentences to collect UK calibration responses and as regression covariates. The iNews corpus, participant pool, and LLM prediction task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The same seven LLMs participate in corresponding modality/persona comparisons, and the regression comparator set is retained. V1 Tables 2 and 7 correspond to v2 Tables 3 and 8. The added ANET comparison concerns annotation calibration.

E3.justification: The added calibration evaluation compares participant ratings with ANET norms converted to a seven-point scale. The LLM protocol retains 30 annotators, 579 test samples, 32-post demonstration pools, and the same metrics. Newly disclosed randomization and quality checks do not establish revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 3 adds a validation analysis testing whether annotators apply the SAM scales consistently with ANET norms, alongside attention-check outcomes. Existing modality and persona analyses, the pilot, supplementary regressions, and qualitative questionnaire analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new calibration table follows the mean-and-standard-deviation reporting already used in v1. Existing significance tests and standard-deviation error bars are retained; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports 4.67 minutes of average instruction-reading time, 7/291 attention-check failures, and calibration means and standard deviations. For example, Table 1 reports arousal 6.19 (SD 1.05) against ANET's 6.32 (SD 1.12) for item 6400. Existing model, regression, and pilot results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mixed-effects specifications, R-squared calculations, and effect-size analysis match across v1 Appendix A.7 and v2 Appendix A.8. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The central dataset contribution and claims concerning 15.2% explained variance, persona benefits, few-shot behavior, and modality differences are retained. V2 emphasizes behavioral simulation more prominently, but this application was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets agreement with ANET norms as evidence of correct scale use and discusses demographic differences between the samples. Section 9 newly clarifies that news-evoked affect may differ in nature or intensity from emotions arising from direct lived experiences.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the dataset-link placeholder with concrete Data and Code hyperlinks and includes the full illustrated annotation manual in Appendix A.4. It newly documents randomization, minimum instruction time, comprehension checks, retained-but-flagged attention failures, and ANET licensing restrictions. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ekman (1992), Peer et al. (2022), and LLM psychology studies by Hu, Liu, and Zhu and colleagues. It removes Plutchik (1980), Lerner et al. (2015), and Zadra and Clore (2011). The opening broadens behavioral-simulation positioning while the related-work discussion largely remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening motivation are rewritten around individual behavior, and quality-control and annotation-manual sections are added. The introduction's 'early descent' terminology becomes 'early ascent.' Most analytical prose and the existing section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The new manual substantially expands visual presentation through SAM scale displays, annotation-form screenshots, and four worked examples. V2 also adds the ANET comparison table. Existing figures and tables are retained, with renumbering and several relocations, including Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through the included annotation manual, explicit quality-control handling, and concrete data/code access links. The ANET comparison adds limited validation, and the new applicability qualification improves precision. The overall gain is limited because validation covers three calibration items and the main modeling evidence remains unchanged.
